'''Tsachik Gelander''' ({{Langx|he|צחיק גלנדר}}) is an Israeli mathematician working in the fields of [[Lie groups]], [[topological groups]], [[symmetric spaces]], [[Rigidity (mathematics)|rigidity]], [[Lattice (discrete subgroup)|lattices]] and discrete subgroups (of Lie groups as well as general locally compact groups). He was a professor of mathematics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 2006 until 2013, and has been at the Weizmann Institute of Science from 2013,<ref>{{cite web | title=People &#124; Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science | url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/math/people }}</ref> and at Northwestern University from 2022.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.northwestern.edu/people/faculty/tsachik-gelander.html|title=Yizhaq (Tsachik) Gelander: Department of Mathematics - Northwestern University|website=www.math.northwestern.edu}}</ref>

Gelander earned his PhD from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 2003, under the supervision of [[Shahar Mozes]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=96347}}</ref> His [[Thesis|doctoral dissertation]], ''Counting Manifolds and Tits Alternative'', won the Haim Nessyahu Prize in Mathematics, awarded by the [[Israel Mathematical Union]] for the best annual doctoral dissertation in mathematics.<ref>{{citation|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Haim_Nessyahu_Prize/|title= The Haim Nessyahu Prize in Mathematics|work=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive|accessdate=20 July 2020}}</ref> After holding a Gibbs Assistant Professorship at Yale University, and faculty positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the Weizmann Institute of Science, Gelander joined Northwestern where he is currently a professor of mathematics.<ref name="auto"/> He contributed to the theory of [[Lattice (discrete subgroup)|lattices]], [[Arithmetic Fuchsian group|Fuchsian groups]] and [[local rigidity]], and the work on [[Chern's conjecture (affine geometry)|Chern's conjecture]] and the Derivation Problem.<ref>{{citation|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/mathematics-mapping-a-fixed-point/|title= Mathematics: Mapping a fixed point|date= 22 November 2011|last1= Guérin|first1= Nicolas}} EPFL</ref> Among his well-known results is the solution to the Goldman conjecture, i.e.    that the action of <math>Out(F_n)</math> on the deformation variety of a compact Lie group is ergodic when <math>n</math> is at least <math>3</math>.

He gave the distinguished Nachdiplom Lectures at ETH Zurich in 2011, and was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], giving a talk under the title of ''Asymptotic Invariants of Locally Symmetric Spaces.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jEvXF6bR9U8|title=Asymptotic invariants of locally symmetric spaces – Tsachik Gelander – ICM2018|date=28 September 2018|via=YouTube}}</ref> He was one of the recipients of the first call of the European Research Council (ERC) Starting Grant (2007), and in 2021 he won the ERC Advanced Grant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc-2021-adg-results-all-domains.pdf|title=ERC Advanced Grants 2021 - List of Principal Investigators}}</ref>
